# mt2.time.set

Set pause and speed, then read them back.

```lua
mt2.time.set(paused: boolean, speed?: number): MT2Clock
```

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paused` | `boolean` | `Required` | Whether simulation is paused. |
| `speed` | `number` | `1` | Native simulation speed. |

## Contract

- **Returns:** MT2Clock
- **Thread:** Framework callbacks; native object/camera/time reads verify the game thread.
- **When to call:** Active callbacks. Game-dependent calls reject during script preparation and start.
- **Effects:** Changes simulation time; local multiplayer class is not allowed.
- **Reload:** Subscriptions owned by the old instance are removed on a successful replacement.
- **Persistence:** No implicit persistence.
- **Capabilities:** `time.write`
- **Since:** 1.0.0
- **Stability:** stable-within-api-1

## Errors

- Invalid speed, unavailable world and shared writes without the multiplayer bridge are rejected.
- Framework 0.2.0 requires acknowledged standalone or trusted Host authority; Unknown and Client never execute the request.
- An invalid or failing experimental api.time.set writer rejects before the original request. Existing multiplayer bridge fences still apply.

## Example

This complete example is also available under `examples/time/main.lua` in the source and SDK documentation bundle. Native effects require the real game.

```lua
-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
mt2.ui.window("Time", function()
    if not mt2.world.status().loaded then return end
    local clock = mt2.time.get()
    mt2.ui.text("Day: " .. clock.day)
    if mt2.ui.button("Pause") then mt2.time.set(true, 1) end
    if mt2.ui.button("Resume") then mt2.time.set(false, 1) end
end)
```
